_comment: Peak-bagging lists, as data rather than code — the same rule Courses/ follows, so completing
a list is a file drop and not a release. Every row is one summit: display name, elevation in
feet as its list publishes it, and the summit coordinate used to decide whether a hike reached
INCOMPLETE ON PURPOSE. colorado14ers carries 9 of its 58. Only rows verified against a source
are here; the rest are absent rather than guessed, because these numbers get printed on a wall
and a remembered elevation is not a fact. The gap is load-bearing: PeakCatalog reports the list
as incomplete, and the 14ers poster stays unlisted until the count matches — the same rule the
medal frame and the hanger follow. Fill in the remaining 49 and the product turns itself on.
One reason not to trust memory here, found while writing this file: Torreys Peak is 14,267 ft
on its source and 14,275 ft in several secondary lists. Eight feet is nothing on a mountain and
everything on a poster someone paid for.
